gaps.sentence: ___ of my two brothers work in banking.
gaps.explanation: 'Both of my two brothers work ...' is correct; 'all' and 'none' are not used for two.

gaps.hint: general statement without 'the' — 'people' has no article
gaps.explanation: 'Most people' means people in general; 'most of' needs 'the' (most of the people).

gaps.sentence: We haven't got ___ chairs for everyone.
gaps.explanation: 'Enough chairs' means a sufficient number; 'too' before the noun would give the wrong meaning and position.

gaps.sentence: ___ the students passed with good grades.
gaps.explanation: Before 'the + noun' use 'most of': 'Most of the students'; 'most the students' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: There are trees on ___ side of the road.
gaps.hint: singular noun: each of the two sides
gaps.explanation: 'Either side' means each of the two sides; 'both' would need the plural 'sides'.

gaps.sentence: I put ___ sugar in your tea by mistake.
gaps.explanation: 'Too much' is used before uncountable nouns like sugar; 'too sugar' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: I don't like this colour — do you have it in ___ colours?
gaps.explanation: 'Other colours' uses 'other' as an adjective before the plural noun; 'another' is followed by singular nouns.
'Some' is used in offers and requests where we expect agreement; 'any' is for neutral questions.
